Q: Optimisation peptide molecule structure in RdKit environment A: 
from rdkit import rdBase
print('Version : ', rdBase.rdkitVersion)
print('boostVersion : ', rdBase.boostVersion)


from rdkit import Chem
from rdkit.Chem import AllChem
from rdkit.Chem import rdDepictor
from rdkit.Chem import Draw

aa_seq = "GDYSHASPLRYPEGGG"
pep = Chem.MolFromSequence(aa_seq)
pep = Chem.AddHs(pep)
drug_smiles = "CCCC1SC[C@]2(C)NC(=O)N[C@]12C"
drug = Chem.MolFromSmiles(drug_smiles)
drug = Chem.AddHs(drug)


AllChem.EmbedMolecule(drug, useRandomCoords=True) #works
# AllChem.EmbedMolecule(drug) #, randomSeed=123)         #works
# AllChem.MMFFOptimizeMolecule(drug)                  ### what difference makes ??

AllChem.EmbedMolecule(pep, useRandomCoords=True)    #works
# AllChem.EmbedMolecule(pep, randomSeed=123)        #doesnt works ValueError: Bad Conformer Id in AllChem.MMFFOptimizeMolecule(pep) 
# AllChem.MMFFOptimizeMolecule(pep)                 ### what difference makes ??
    

pep_conf=pep.GetNumConformers()

print('\n\npep conformer : ' , pep_conf)

print(pep.GetNumConformers(),pep.GetConformer().Is3D())

AllChem.MMFFOptimizeMolecule(pep)


Draw.MolToFile(pep, "pep_just_draw.png", size=(1200,1200))

Draw.MolToFile(drug, "drug_just_draw.png", size=(1200,1200))
    
    
pepsmi = Chem.MolToSmiles(pep)

drugsmi = Chem.MolToSmiles(drug)

print('pep smiles :', pepsmi)

print('\n\ndrug smiles :', drugsmi)

pep = Chem.RemoveHs(pep)
drug = Chem.RemoveHs(drug)

bonded = Chem.CombineMols(pep, drug)


edbonded = Chem.RWMol(bonded)

# 4. Add bond between pep atom 0 and drug atom 0 (now index +pep.GetNumAtoms())
edbonded.AddBond(0, 0+pep.GetNumAtoms(), order=Chem.rdchem.BondType.SINGLE)
conjugate = edbonded

#####################################################################
# without this I cannot go further .... ---> conjugate = Chem.AddHs(conjugate, explicitOnly=False , addCoords=True)
#                                            RuntimeError: Pre-condition Violation
#                                            getNumImplicitHs() called without preceding call to calcImplicitValence()
rdDepictor.Compute2DCoords(conjugate)
# conjugate_conf=conjugate.GetNumConformers() # not needed
###################################################################


conjugate = Chem.AddHs(conjugate, explicitOnly=False , addCoords=True)

     
conjugatesmi= Chem.MolToSmiles(conjugate)

print('\n\nconjugate smiles :', conjugatesmi)


############# without this is the pdb I get is flat 2D #######
AllChem.EmbedMolecule(conjugate, useRandomCoords=True)
# AllChem.MMFFOptimizeMolecule(conjugate)       ### what difference makes ??
# conjugate_conf=conjugate.GetNumConformers()
#############################################################

Draw.MolToFile(conjugate, "conjugate_just_draw.png", size=(1200,1200))

import sys

Chem.MolToPDBFile(conjugate, sys.path[0]+"conjugate.pdb")

Not sure if answer is what you where looking for because I don't know the default value of randomseed keyword in EmbedMolecule func, anyway in my attemps I get akways different results *** see ADDENDUM below

ADDENDUMhttps://www.rdkit.org/docs/GettingStartedInPython.html#chem-vs-allchem

Google more and found out that:

rdkit.Chem.AllChem.EmbedMolecule is equivalent to rdkit.Chem.rdDistGeom.EmbedMolecule ; Chem vs AllChem

and the function is nicely explained at rdkit.Chem.rdDistGeom.EmbedMolecule where randomseed defaults to -1 and as in argument explanation

randomSeedprovide a seed for the random number generator

so that the same coordinates can be obtained for a molecule on multiple runs. If -1, the RNG will not be seeded.

but there is more here

EmbedMolecule() is no longer random?

so I get different conformers because each time I re-run my script default randomseed = -1 the RNG (random number generator) will not be seeded

if I change :

AllChem.EmbedMolecule(drug, useRandomCoords=True) #works AllChem.EmbedMolecule(pep, useRandomCoords=True) #works

to

AllChem.EmbedMolecule(drug,randomSeed=1234, useRandomCoords=True) #works AllChem.EmbedMolecule(pep,,randomSeed=1234, useRandomCoords=True) #works

I will end up with the same conformer/result.

NOW I'll have to investigate useRandomCoords=True and check why using useRandomCoords=False fails, but only fr the peptide and not the drug

Q: C++ Kill a Thread In Destructor A:

If you want a thread to die, you should ask it to exit. It's the only reliable way to do it cleanly.

Just change

while (true)

to

while(this->keepRunning)

and synchronize it appropriately. Either don't detach the thread (so the destructor can join it) or add some way for the thread to indicate that it has exited (so the destructor can wait for it).

Oh, and instead of spinning, the thread should probably sleep. In that case, if you don't want the destructor to also block, you need some way to interrupt the sleep: using a timed wait on a condition variable for your sleep makes this easy.

Late edit: since it was already 2020 when I answered this, I should probably have pointed out std::stop_source & friends as a sensible default approach.

Q: How do I create a null value (skip a cell) when entering a literal array in Google Sheets? A:

while this was possible to do in pre-2013 era nowadays this is NOT possible to do so in scope you describe it

parse error you were getting can be now run just fine:

=ARRAYFORMULA(HSTACK(LEFT(A2:A), RIGHT(A2:A), , MID(D2:D, 2, 1)))

but this will still not allow you to enter manual input in those empty columns without braking the formula.

one way to do this is to have arrayformula columns separated from manual input columns. you would put your formulae into a service row using VSTACK and then either hide the service row or change height of that row to 2px. example:

B1:

=IFNA(VSTACK(, HSTACK(LEFT(A2:A), RIGHT(A2:A))))

D column manual input

E column manual input

F1:

=IFNA(VSTACK(, MID(D2:D, 2, 1)))

then hide or shrink row 1
